title: 6 days french bodybuilding split review
summary: NH reviews a French viewer's six-day bodybuilding split (6 ft, about 95 kg, near 350 lb bench). He approves most days and rep ranges but suggests evolving sets instead of 5x3 or 6x3 heavy work, adding chin-ups, face pulls, skull crushers, shrugs and hyperextensions, and cutting redundant biceps isolation in favor of heavy strict EZ bar curls, with supersets to shorten sessions.
claims: Five sets of three on bench drifts toward sandbagging; switch to 3x5 or keep triples with an evolving set range of 3-5 sets
The incline bench is a bastardized lift between horizontal and overhead press; he isn't a fan but 6-10 reps is a good range for it and close-grip bench
Avoid rep ranges that push flies to mechanical failure; like good mornings, failure there is pointless and risks pec tendon or shoulder
A 10-20 rep range is too wide for only three sets; it fits four sets better
He cannot do dumbbell curls with both arms at once; he always alternates
Add chin-ups to a chest and arms day, supersetted with incline bench, for more vertical pulling which you can never do too much of
Band flies after horizontal pressing let him target the upper chest because the lower chest is already exhausted
Squatting the day after heavy pressing can be hard for people with tight shoulders
Light shoulder work the day after a heavy day, hitting different heads, may speed recovery
RDLs respond well to 6-10 reps and even 15, because you can grind them
For legs, swap rigid 6x3 squats for something like 4-6 sets of 3-9 reps to widen volume options
Calves at 3x10-15 must be weighted; otherwise there is not enough tonnage for them to respond
Lateral and rear delt work after squats can alleviate post-squat shoulder pain
Yates rows at 8-12 are perfect: heavy enough but controllable to stretch the lats
Upper back growth is limited by shoulder, biceps and elbow tendons and lower back integrity; anything hitting the upper back without stressing those, go ham
The back is the one muscle where a bro-split day makes sense because it takes huge tonnage from many angles; triceps don't need that many exercises
Close-grip bench works the chest through a longer range; open arm days with a compound like close-grip, pin or board press
Incline curls stretch too far, and high reps on them mostly produce artificial lactic-acid failure
Try strict EZ bar curls for 4 sets of 3-7 reps with a controlled negative for a few months, replacing two or three biceps isolations
Four biceps exercises in one arm day is redundant and too much exercise selection
Arm day restructure: close-grip bench supersetted with EZ skull crushers, EZ curls with face pulls, then triceps extensions with hammer curls and reverse flies, roughly halving session time
Start the week with an upper body day to fire up the body before the leg day
Do ab isolation every day if you want bigger abs
Many of his viewers do almost as much lower body tonnage as upper, which is fine
Without floor pulls, add hyperextensions for lower back and hamstrings
The triceps long head can take more volume than the lateral and medial heads and is key for big arms
Shrugs are easy to superset with anything if you want bigger traps
Strength that you can keep pushing is what a bodybuilder needs
exercises: bastardized press; ok if shoulders tolerate
